---
title: "Code quality"
---

The agent keeps slipping `print()` into production modules instead of using your logger, and bare `except:` clauses show up under deadline pressure. You want layered feedback. Two structural checks fire on every edit, a behavioral nudge reacts when the agent's narration repeats the antipattern, and a final LLM gate handles ambiguous cases.

<!-- gd-embed: code_quality.py -->

The same problem expressed at four escalating tiers, all firing on `Event.PostToolUse`. The first `hook(...)` uses the [`Pattern`](../reference/index.qmd) condition, where `Pattern("print($$$)")` matches a real print call, never a `print(` inside a string or comment, more precise than the regex it replaces. The `lint(bare_excepts, ...)` check walks the Python AST for a bare `except:`, the `ExceptHandler.type is None` case, a Python-specific fact no pattern string expresses. That is why it stays an `ast` check instead of ast-grep. `nudge(... signals=...)` watches transcript narration to catch the agent talking about the antipattern, and `llm_gate(...)` lets a model adjudicate the ambiguous prod-print cases. A condition answers yes or no. When you want each violation located by line and scoped to the changed lines, reach for [`ast_grep_rule`](styleguide.qmd) and `styleguide()`. See also [primitives](../guide/primitives.qmd) and [LLM hooks](../guide/llm-hooks.qmd) for the full set.
